title: The business plan
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Why a business plan matters, covers the plan's purpose and its use with lenders but not the contents the new point requires (idea, market, competitors, marketing, staffing and finances), so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: The business plan
card: A business plan is a written document that sets out how a new business will start and run.
It describes the business idea and its goals. It also covers the market, the competitors and the marketing.
It also explains staffing needs and the finances, such as expected costs and income.
The owner uses it as a guide for decisions. Lenders often ask to see one before they agree to lend money.
draft.remember: A business plan is the owner's written map, and lenders often want to read it.

a.q: Why might a bank ask Leila to show a business plan before she borrows money for her new florist shop?
opts: To judge whether the business can succeed and repay
To set the prices Leila must charge customers
To choose which staff Leila must hire
To decide the shop's opening hours for her
a.why: A plan sets out the market, competitors and finances, so the bank can judge if the business is likely to repay. Banks do not set prices or choose staff. The owner makes those choices and records them in the plan.
a.clue: Think about what a lender wants to be sure of.

b.q: Sam is writing a plan for a food truck in Bendigo. He lists the trucks that already sell lunch nearby. Which part of the plan is this?
b.why: Other food trucks selling to the same customers are competitors. Staffing covers the people Sam needs to hire, and finances cover costs and income.
b.clue: Who else is trying to win the same customers?

a.best: To judge whether the business can succeed and repay
